body:
Looks good!


The FoldableContainer font hover color is too close to the collapsed font color. But that's not really an issue with this PR.

Some feedback from a usability perspective: - The 'show replace' button in front of the search is pretty bad usability. At the surface, nothing hints at that button enabling the 'replace' mode of the find in files panel. Here's a mockup / suggestion for what I think is a better design and which I don't think takes a lot of rework on the UI: … and with replace disabled, hiding the field: - I see no reason for the 'Filters' section to be foldable, and folded in by default. The big empty space upon first opening the panel feels pretty useless. Might as well remove the foldable state, keep the filters as a header, and have it unfolded at all times. (already in the above mockup) - The checkboxes for what files to search are unfortunately positioned under the 'Excludes' property which feels like a header, creating a bit of a false sense that the checkboxes are for files to ignore. best move those checkboxes under the 'Includes' property instead. (already in the mockup above) - Once there's tabs, I'd expect the 'create new tab' button (the button with the plus icon) to move to the right of the tabs: … and now that I'm thinking about it, why not just always have tabs, even when there's a single one, and add the create button next to the right-most tab? Then there doesn't have to be any fiddling with the create tab button at all. - The 'replace' and 'remove result' buttons on the right of the results lack hover states:

Tested the PR again and most of my earlier usability concerns were addressed! Good work @TheDying0fLight! Approving this, though there's a few more nitpicks that could also be addressed in a followup PR: - there's a lot of margin here for some reason, a lot more than on the left side of that same subpanel: - for clarity's sake, I think we should consider adding a **Find:** header / label above the find input field. Right now it's just a kind of floating text input field that, if there's a bit of text in there, doesn't immediately communicate that it is the most important field of the whole panel ;) Properties always have their labels in front of then no matter what for good reason. The replace field now just happens to have it because of the checkbox above, making the lack of label on the find find text input field even more of a glaring omission. - for consistency's sake, maybe rename the placeholder of the find input field from "Search" to "Find". - also for consistency: the placeholders in the include and exclude fields should either be capitalized, or the placeholders in the find and replace fields should not.
